document.title: Northern Afghan Strongman General Dostam Meets Taliban Representatives (Islama 00975)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Pakistan: "The Taliban's Godfather"?
document.note: [Confidential] Pakistani officials allegedly tell Gen. Dostum not to worry about the Taliban because Pakistan can take care of them, and he reportedly agrees to cooperate with the Taliban on opening trade routes. Taliban officials tell him they have no territorial ambitions in the north. The Taliban would seize Mazar-e-Sharif in May 1997.

persons.name: Abdur-Rashid Dostam
persons.role: Northern Afghan strongman and general based in Mazar-i-Sharif

mentions.quote: MEETING BETWEEN GENERAL ABDUR-RASHID DOSTAM AND REPRESENTATIVES OF THE TALIBAN IN MAZAR-I-SHARIF
DURING DOSTAM'S VISIT TO ISLAMABAD IN DECEMBER, PAKISTANI GOVERNMENT OFFICIALS REPORTEDLY HAD TOLD DOSTAM NOT TO CONSIDER AN ALLIANCE WITH AHMED SHAH MASOOD

persons.name: Ahmed Shah Masood
persons.role: Afghan government military commander; Pakistani officials urged Dostam not to ally with him

mentions.quote: TOLD DOSTAM NOT TO CONSIDER AN ALLIANCE WITH AHMED SHAH MASOOD, AND TO INSTEAD MAINTAIN HIS LINKS WITH HEKMATYAR

persons.name: Gulbuddin Hekmatyar
persons.role: Afghan faction leader; Dostam's link; potential threat to seize Kabul

mentions.quote: ENSURE THAT HEKMATYAR DOES NOT SEIZE THE CAPITAL

organizations.name: Taliban
organizations.notes: Sent representatives to Dostam in Mazar-i-Sharif in early December 1994; stated no territorial ambitions in the north and intent to declare Kabul an open city.

organizations.name: Government of Pakistan
organizations.notes: Reportedly advised Dostam against allying with Masood, said it could take care of the Taliban, and agreed to continue limited financial aid to Dostam.

organizations.name: U.S. Embassy Islamabad
organizations.notes: Author of the cable; the POLOFF received reports from unnamed sources.

places.name: Mazar-i-Sharif
places.significance: Dostam's base and site of the Taliban-Dostam meeting.

places.name: Islamabad
places.significance: Site of Dostam's December meetings with Pakistani officials.

places.name: Kandahar-Kabul road
places.significance: Taliban aimed to open it; Dostam asked to cooperate if they did.

places.name: Salang Tunnel
places.significance: Dostam asked to open it and the northern road; vital to Pakistan's Central Asian trade.

places.name: Kabul
places.significance: Taliban said they would declare it an open city.

events.description: Several Taliban, accompanied by two unidentified Pakistanis, called on Dostam in Mazar-i-Sharif; told him they had no territorial ambitions in the north and asked him not to oppose them.
Dostam visited Islamabad where Pakistani officials reportedly urged him to avoid an alliance with Masood, keep links with Hekmatyar, and open the Salang road.
A source told the POLOFF that Mazar sources had shared the gist of Dostam's Islamabad meetings, and that Dostam reportedly agreed to the requests.
Taliban representatives, with two unidentified Pakistanis, call on General Dostam in Mazar-i-Sharif and ask him not to oppose them and to open the Salang road.
Dostam visits Islamabad and meets Pakistani officials, who advise against an alliance with Masood and for keeping ties with Hekmatyar.
A source tells the U.S. Embassy Poloff that Mazar-i-Sharif sources shared the gist of Dostam's Islamabad meetings, and that Dostam reportedly agreed to the Pakistani requests.
U.S. Embassy Islamabad sends the cable reporting the Taliban-Dostam meeting to Washington.

sources_cited: Unnamed source in a foreign government who spoke to the U.S. Embassy POLOFF, claiming excellent sources within the Dostam camp
key_claims: Taliban representatives, accompanied by two unidentified Pakistanis, told Dostam in early December 1994 that they had no territorial ambitions in the north.
The Taliban asked Dostam to open the Salang Tunnel and northern road and keep Hekmatyar out of Kabul if the Kandahar-Kabul road opened.
Pakistani officials reportedly told Dostam Pakistan could take care of the Taliban.
Pakistan allegedly urged Dostam to keep his links with Hekmatyar and avoid an alliance with Masood.
Pakistan reportedly agreed to continue limited financial assistance to Dostam in return for opening the Salang road, which was vital to its planned Central Asian trade.
Dostam reportedly agreed to the Pakistani requests.
